---
title: "Course support"
---

## Lectures and labs

If you have a question during lecture or lab, feel free to ask it! There are likely other students with the same question, so by asking you will create a learning opportunity for everyone.

## Office hours

Office hours are available by appointment at [this link](https://calendly.com/vanderplas-stat/office-hours). In general, office hours will be via Zoom - this allows me to offer more availability, and doesn't require you to come to campus to visit my office.

If you'd prefer to meet in person, try to schedule your appointment on a class day (ideally within ~2 hours of class, and not on Friday afternoon), and mention in the request that you want an in-person meeting. I will let you know if that's feasible given my schedule for the day. 

## Email

Please only use email for questions about personal matters that may not be appropriate for the public course forum (e.g., illness, grades, accommodations, etc.). 
In these cases, please add "STAT1080" to the subject line, so that I can prioritize your email.

Assignment and content related questions should be asked in the relevant discussion board on Canvas.

## Academic support

There are times you may need help with the class that is beyond what can be provided by the teaching team. In those instances, I encourage you to visit the [**Academic Support Hub**](https://www.usu.edu/academic-support/), which offers free support to all students. You can learn better study skills, how to take notes effectively, how to reinforce your learning, and how to monitor how well you do and do not know a topic. This will help you not only in this class, but in every class you take down the road. 

## Mental health and wellness

Your mental health and wellness extremely important, and the university offers resources to support students in managing daily stress and self-care. UNL offers several resources for students to manage stress, seek help with well-being, and access crisis and long-term care.

-   [Counseling and Prevention Services (CAPS)](https://www.usu.edu/aggiewellness/caps/) operates M-F 8-5 and can be reached at 435-797-1012

-   [Survivor Support, Advocacy, and Violence Intervention](https://www.usu.edu/ssavi/),  (435) 797-7273. TSC 311. SSAVI provides  support and resources for victims/survivors of interpersonal violence.

-   [Disability Resource Center (DRC)](https://www.usu.edu/drc/), [drc\@usu.edu](mailto://drc@usu.edu?subject="Initial help") or (435) 797-2444 -- resources for students experiencing short or long-term disabilities that affect the campus or educational experience.

## Technology

Students who do not have a working computer can check out a loaner laptop from USU Academic Support Services. 

1. Contact [USU IT Service Support](https://it.usu.edu/service-desk) about availability for the semester.
2. Use the Laptop Loan Program Form on the right side of the [Academic Support](https://www.usu.edu/academic-support/space_tech/index) page under "Additional Supports" at the bottom of the list.

If you are unable to get a loaner laptop set up with the software required for parts of this course, please try to let me know ahead of time - it is possible that I will be able to assist you with browser-based solutions or that I can bring an extra laptop or tablet that can access a browser-based solution. 
This is not a guarantee, but I'm a nerd and I sometimes have extra laptops laying around that can be temporarily repurposed for class. 

## Course materials

There are no costs associated with this course beyond the requirement that you have access to a laptop computer. 
All readings will come from freely available, open resources (open-source textbooks, journal articles, etc.) or library course reserves.
